records.title: TGF-β Inhibition Attenuates Tau Accumulation and Neurodegeneration in Progressive Supranuclear Palsy Patient-Derived Organoids.
records.abstract: Progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) is a devastating 4-repeat tauopathy with no approved disease-modifying treatments. Recent evidence showed increased transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) levels in PSP patient-derived ventral midbrain organoids (vMOs) and serum neuronally derived exosomes. This study investigated whether TGF-β pharmacological inhibition could mitigate PSP pathology in vMOs. Ninety-six vMOs were generated from induced pluripotent stem cells from two PSP-Richardson's syndrome patients and two healthy control donors (HCs). From day 60 to day 90, PSP organoids were (1) exposed to TGF-β receptor I inhibitor (SB431542); (2) exposed to recombinant TGF-β1, TGF-β2, and TGF-β3; or (3) untreated. At day 90, several tau species were assessed by immunoblotting; neurodegeneration was evaluated through TUNEL assay and immunofluorescence (tyrosine hydroxylase [TH], neurofilament light chain [NfL]); astrocytic activation (glial fibrillary acidic protein [GFAP]) marker was evaluated by immunofluorescence, and histopathological hallmarks were evaluated by immunohistochemistry. An HC-derived organoid subgroup was exposed to the treatment conditions to assess potential toxicity. At day 90, untreated PSP-derived vMOs exhibited increased phosphorylated tau levels (Ser396, Thr181, Ser202/Ser205 [AT8]) compared with HC-derived vMOs, dopaminergic neuron loss (reduced TH, increased NfL), and astrocytic reactivity (increased GFAP), along with PSP characteristic tau deposition. Tau hyperphosphorylation, neurodegeneration, and astrocytic reactivity were all markedly reduced in PSP-derived vMOs treated with TGF-β receptor I inhibitor. Conversely, exposure to TGF-β exacerbated these features. No toxic effects were observed in HC vMOs exposed to treatment conditions. Pharmacological inhibition of TGF-β signaling prevented key PSP molecular alterations in patient-derived organoids. These findings support further research and pave the way for future investigation of TGF-β-targeting strategies in clinical trials in patients with PSP. © 2026 The Author(s). records.title: Niches in cancer: from primary tumors to metastatic disease.
records.abstract: Cancer progression does not occur in isolation: malignant-cell states and fates are shaped by specialized microenvironments, or cancer niches. Within primary tumors, vascular, stromal, immune and neural interactions create local hypoxic, metabolic and mechanical conditions that together influence malignant-cell behavior. These local environments sustain stem-like states, regulate immune surveillance and vascular remodeling, and influence dissemination and treatment response. Tumor-derived extracellular vesicles and other systemic signals connect primary tumors to distant organs, conditioning tissues before tumor-cell arrival and subsequently modulating disseminated tumor-cell seeding, dormancy, reactivation and outgrowth. Cancer niches therefore operate across spatial scales and disease stages, shaping tumor behavior in ways that cannot be explained by tumor-cell-intrinsic properties alone. Advances in single-cell and spatial profiling, organoid systems and intravital imaging are revealing their cellular composition, local architecture and evolution. In this review, we integrate primary, pre-metastatic and metastatic niche biology, examine how local environments evolve and influence one another during cancer progression, compare organ-specific metastatic niches and assess emerging therapeutic strategies. Effective niche-directed therapy will require identifying the interactions that sustain disease, showing that treatment disrupts them and determining which patients are most likely to benefit. Greater spatial, temporal and functional resolution may reveal new therapeutic vulnerabilities and create opportunities to prevent relapse and achieve more durable disease control.

records.title: The Importance of Translational Research for Neurodevelopmental Disorders and Autism Spectrum Disorders.
records.abstract: Translational research is the process of transforming fundamental biological discoveries into safe and efficacious interventions for patients. This specialized field is of particular importance for neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs), a broad class of behaviorally defined conditions including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDDs), and related disorders. NDDs present unique translational challenges including (i) a lack of biological diagnostic markers; (ii) the fact that they are diagnosed exclusively by behavioral criteria; (iii) their involvement of dysfunction in complex brain circuitry; and (iv) that there is no single unifying biological mechanism. This chapter reviews the current landscape of translational neuroscience for NDDs, examining the strengths and limitations of preclinical model systems, including rodent models humanized mice, human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) 3D spheroids and brain organoids. This work emphasizes that research emanating from the varying preclinical experimental systems above should be leveraged and their complementary strengths integrated, coordinated, and considered collaboratively, to strengthen current knowledge, identify the remaining research gaps, and prioritize future research. We also emphasize the importance of rigorous, reproducible methodology and conservative interpretation of behavioral and functional outcomes. Discussion is presented on key translational bridges or connections that are urgently required to advance the field: bridging non-human model systems to humanized models, identifying and validating translational biomarkers, bridging in vitro and in vivo findings, and developing corroborative alternatives to animal models. It is our stance that integrating multiple complementary model systems, limiting erroneous behavioral inferences, relying on evolutionarily conserved circuits, and prioritizing robust and reproducible outcome measures will reduce failures in the translational pipeline and accelerate the development of meaningful therapies for individuals with NDDs.

records.title: Organotypic vascularization improves maturation of human stem cell-derived islets and restores normoglycemia in diabetic mice.
records.abstract: Human pluripotent stem cells-derived pancreatic islet organoids (PIOs) hold promise for treating type 1 diabetes, but poor post-transplant survival due to inadequate vascularization remains a major challenge. Here, we generated vascularized PIOs (VPIOs) by co-culturing PIOs with blood vessel organoids (BVOs), resulting in integrated structures with BVOs-derived capillary networks that penetrate into the islet structures. These blood vessels structurally exhibit fenestrations characteristic of islet-specific endothelium and carry a molecular signature of organotypic vasculature. β cells within the VPIOs display partially enhanced maturation and greater resistance to hypoxia and endoplasmic reticulum stress. Following subcutaneous transplantation into diabetic mice, VPIOs exhibit markedly improved survival, establish vascular connections with the host circulation, and restore long-term normoglycemia. Our work presents a strategy for generating vascularized islet organoids that enhances β cell maturation and tissue-specific blood vessel specification in vitro and, critically, improves graft survival and function in vivo.

records.title: BMP4 and ERK signaling favor endothelial over smooth muscle differentiation through counteracting TGF-β signaling.
records.abstract: Vascular cells hold great potential not only for treating vascular disease but also for engineering vascularized organoids and tissues for transplantation. Both endothelial cells (ECs) and smooth muscle cells (SMCs) can be derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) via intermediate vascular progenitors (VPs). Our previous study showed that the VPs generated from hiPSCs using VEGF, FGF2, and BMP4 can efficiently differentiate into ECs. In this study, we found that BMP4 favored EC differentiation at the cost of SMC differentiation. Interestingly, inhibition of the TGF-β signaling by small molecule SB431542 or SB525334, could also induce EC differentiation while suppress SMC differentiation. In addition, both BMP4 and the TGF-β inhibitors activated SMAD1, suggesting that the TGF-β signaling counteracts with the BMP4 signaling. Furthermore, blocking the ERK signaling pathway with an inhibitor U0126 promoted SMC differentiation and inhibited EC differentiation likely through inhibiting the activation of SMAD1 and stimulating SMAD2. Indeed, the treatment of U0126 upregulated the expression of TGF-β2. Importantly, TGF-β inhibitor SB431542 effectively rescued EC differentiation impaired by ERK inhibition, likely through maintaining KDR-mediated VEGF signaling and restricting TGF-β2 signaling. Collectively, our findings highlight the competitive interplay among BMP4, TGF-β and ERK signaling pathways in determining EC versus SMC differentiation.

records.title: Beyond the Transcriptome: The m6A Epitranscriptome in Bovine Mastitis.
records.abstract: Bovine mastitis is a heterogeneous inflammatory disease that compromises milk production, animal welfare and dairy sustainability. Despite extensive transcriptomic and epigenomic research, a PubMed search completed in September 2026 identified only 12 primary studies addressing epitranscriptomic regulation in bovine mastitis, representing approximately 0.1% of indexed publications. This review critically evaluates N6-methyladenosine (m6A), the most extensively studied RNA modification in bovine mastitis, its regulatory machinery and effects on mammary immunity, while identifying m5C and A-to-I editing as priorities for mechanistic investigation. Current evidence identifies transcript-specific RNA stability as the best-supported mechanism and provides a foundation for investigating m6A-dependent translation. Functional studies of ALKBH5-LOC4191, YTHDF2-IER3, YTHDF2-associated CCL20 and CCL5 regulation, m6A-regulated LncRNA7825 and FTO-FN1 demonstrate that m6A reshapes inflammatory signalling, mitochondrial stress, epithelial-barrier integrity, cell survival and bacterial control. Synthesizing these findings, we propose a context-dependent RNA-fate checkpoint model in which biological effects depend on the modified transcript, effector protein, pathogen, cellular context and infection phase. The FTO-FN1 axis shows that bacterial control and tissue protection can diverge, establishing them as complementary outcomes. Future studies should test whether m6A provides an early post-transcriptional response layer and whether pathogens manipulate it, using time-resolved multi-omics, nucleotide-specific perturbation, primary cells, mammary organoids and longitudinal cattle samples. Parallel profiling of non-m6A modifications should define interacting regulatory layers. These approaches should establish causal modification sites, resolve pathogen-specific regulation, connect molecular mechanisms with disease trajectories, and support validated milk-based biomarkers, mammary-targeted interventions and prioritization of stable genetic variants for breeding mastitis-resistant cattle.

records.title: Emerging frontiers for AI in single-cell genomics.
records.abstract: We are just over a decade into the single-cell revolution in biology, which has been coupled to the growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in single-cell genomics. Most early single-cell RNA embedding models and subsequent "foundation models"-representational models pretrained on large single-cell datasets-did not gain wide traction among experimental biologists. However, as massive single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) atlas efforts ramp up, there is a clear rationale for exploiting AI models to interpret new datasets in the context of vast existing data resources. Meanwhile, the advent of single-cell epigenetic/multiomic assays and Perturb-seq technologies presents new opportunities for AI modeling. Here, we review AI embedding and foundation models for scRNA-seq and single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (scATAC-seq), extensive machine-learning efforts to exploit single-cell multiome in regulatory genomics, and AI strategies to learn "virtual cell" models from Perturb-seq, ending with a description of current limitations of single-cell AI models and an outlook for future advances.

records.title: Dynamic Graph Prior-Guided Latent Adaptation for Generalizable Single-Cell Perturbation Response Prediction.
records.abstract: Predicting transcriptional responses to drug perturbations in unseen cellular contexts is a central challenge in single-cell perturbation modeling. This challenge creates a need for models that combine flexible state transitions with structured biological prior knowledge. Existing data-driven models often struggle to generalize across unseen cell types, while many prior-based models rely on static biological graphs without explicitly conditioning prior influence on perturbation-specific target support. We propose DGP-LA, a dynamic graph-prior latent adaptation framework that refines biological priors and injects them as gated latent corrections within a cell-state-conditioned transition model. DGP-LA couples a transition backbone with perturbation-conditioned sparse graph refinement. It propagates gene-aligned target support over the refined graph and selectively injects the resulting topology-aware signal into the hidden representation. On Tahoe and NeurIPS, DGP-LA improves Pearson Delta relative to State by 8.7% and 35.8% for generalization across unseen cell types. In zero-shot drug perturbation response prediction on unseen cell types, it improves Pearson Delta relative to CRISP by 79.1% and 67.6%. The model also improves DE-gene recovery, response discrimination, and Hallmark pathway recovery, supporting adaptive latent integration of biological priors for more generalizable and biologically interpretable perturbation modeling. DGP-LA's source code and reproducibility materials are available at https://github.com/bieyl/DGP-LA and archived on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22155398. Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

records.title: Benchmarking biological knowledge-graph priors against single-cell foundation models for Perturb-seq prediction.
records.abstract: Perturb-seq prediction increasingly relies on either biological graph priors or single-cell foundation models, but their relative value is difficult to interpret when architectures, split definitions and graph sources vary simultaneously. We benchmarked STRING functional associations and Gene Ontology co-annotation against dense, self-edge-only and exact-degree-rewired supports in one fixed graph-attention backbone, with a separate 200-HVG STRING-GO-control-co-expression sensitivity. Four public Perturb-seq datasets, three nested gene-space scales and three optimisation seeds were evaluated on held-out guide conditions; GEARS, scGPT and Geneformer were evaluated on the same held-out conditions, output-gene panels and Pearson-r metric after model-specific validity checks. At 200 highly variable genes, STRING-GO improved the equal-dataset Pearson r by +0.016 (95% interval [+0.010, +0.022]) relative to dense support. Dataset effects were positive in Adamson (+0.017), Norman (+0.015), Replogle K562 (+0.017) and Replogle RPE1 (+0.014), and 122/200 guide conditions improved (0.61 [0.54,0.68]). The top-20-gene Jaccard difference was +0.009 [+0.006,+0.012]. STRING-GO exceeded self-edge-only support by +0.024 [+0.018,+0.029] and the mean of ten exact-degree rewires by +0.011 [+0.005,+0.017]. The native-panel effect declined from +0.016 at 200 genes to +0.009 at 1000 genes; the 1000-200 interaction was -0.006 [-0.011,-0.002]. The primary graph-support comparison was formulated and conducted during peer-review revision rather than planned as an a priori confirmatory study. All three external models passed implementation-specific checks. Across 36 protocol-matched dataset-scale contrasts, 32 were within the descriptive ±0.030 reference envelope and four were outside, all favouring the external model. These results demonstrate a modest empirical predictive improvement under the evaluated matched protocol; they do not by themselves establish practical biological relevance.

records.title: AI-enabled fungal biomanufacturing: from genome mining to the artificial intelligence virtual cell.
records.abstract: Fungi are important chassis organisms for sustainable biomanufacturing owing to their strong secretion capacity, metabolic diversity, and adaptability to industrial processes. Driven by the rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI), computational approaches that enable machines to learn patterns from data and make predictions, together with omics technologies and synthetic biology, data- and model-driven strategies are increasingly reshaping fungal cell factory design and optimization. This review summarizes recent advances in AI-enabled fungal biomanufacturing, covering AI-assisted genome mining, enzyme and pathway analysis, genome editing, metabolic network modeling, and intelligent fermentation control. The review further highlights the emerging concept of the artificial intelligence virtual cell (AIVC), which integrates multi-omics data, mechanistic modeling, and machine learning-based approaches into a unified multiscale framework for simulating dynamic cellular behaviors. The technical foundations and potential applications of AIVC in fungal metabolic engineering, drug discovery, agriculture, and environmental biotechnology are reviewed. Finally, key challenges-data quality and standardization, cross-scale model integration and interpretability, and the gap between in silico prediction and experimental validation-are highlighted. This review provides a systematic perspective on the role of AI and virtual cell technologies in advancing next generation fungal biotechnology.

records.title: PHAROS: turning single-cell perturbation models into target-directed drug-combination screens.
records.abstract: Combination therapies are central to cancer treatment, but exhaustive screening is impractical. We introduce PHAROS, a framework that turns a pretrained single-cell perturbation model into a target-directed search engine for drug combinations. PHAROS predicts how a cell population changes under a drug, one drug at a time, then chains these predictions together to simulate drug combinations. It scores each simulated outcome against the desired target state and uses a search algorithm to find the most promising combinations, all without retraining the underlying model. Across two independent combinatorial perturbation datasets, PHAROS recovered exact or mechanism-matched two-drug responses in cell lines, both seen and unseen during model training. Its rankings were specific to the requested conversion and were not explained by single-drug effects, additive effects, or shared mechanism of action. In exploratory analyses of patient-derived metastatic HR+/HER2- breast tumors and basal cell carcinoma (BCC), PHAROS prioritized FDA-approved regimens, distinguished combinations by their predicted tumor-versus-immune objective profiles, and nominated pathway-level hypotheses, while explicitly identifying both tumor cohorts as outside the model's supported distribution. PHAROS provides a modular route from pretrained virtual-cell models to inverse, single-cell combination-screening platforms.

records.title: HDAC8 Assistant: a QSAR-guided molecular generation platform for de novo design and virtual screening of HDAC8 inhibitors.
records.abstract: Histone deacetylase 8 (HDAC8) inhibitors are considered promising therapeutic agents for the treatment of cancer and several other diseases. In this study, regression QSAR models for HDAC8 inhibitors were developed using various types of molecular descriptors and machine learning algorithms. The best-performing weighted consensus model achieved an external predictive performance of Q2test = 0.62 for the complete test set and 0.71 for compounds within the applicability domain, covering 77% of the external data. Model reliability was confirmed by five-fold cross-validation and y-randomization tests. The developed QSAR model was integrated into the HDAC8 Assistant web application (https://hdac8-assistant.streamlit.app/), which includes a de novo molecular generation module based on recurrent neural networks (SMILES-RNN) and reinforcement learning (REINVENT 2). For targeted discovery of novel inhibitors, an original reward function was proposed that combines QSAR-predicted activity with applicability domain control for generated compounds. This approach enables simultaneous optimization of predicted inhibitory activity while limiting extrapolation beyond the model applicability domain. HDAC8 Assistant also implements assessment of drug-likeness according to the Muegge criteria, as well as PAINS, toxicophore, and Brenk structural-alert detection. Molecular docking was performed for the most promising compounds generated by HDAC8 Assistant to analyse their interactions with the HDAC8 active site.

records.title: Programming biological behavior with AI-guided de novo protein design.
records.abstract: Driven by advances in artificial intelligence, de novo protein design can now generate diverse molecular functions from the ground up, achieving remarkable success in engineering binders against many macromolecular targets. Here, we provide a perspective on how de novo design can progress beyond bimolecular interactions toward the bottom-up construction of protein reaction networks. We highlight how programmable, modular, and controllable de novo components can drive complex, emergent biological behaviors. Overcoming current challenges-including designable protein dynamics, multi-step functionalities, and non-equilibrium systems-is essential for this transition. With continued foundational method improvements, the field is poised to pioneer precise protein perturbations for systems-level insight and to engineer emergent cellular behaviors like signal amplification, decision-making, and error correction de novo to fundamentally advance synthetic biology, biotechnology, and medicine.

records.title: Multi-Objective Molecular Generation via Actor-Critic Regulated by Adaptive Cooperative Evolution.
records.abstract: Many complex diseases involve intricate and interdependent biological mechanisms, making multi-target drug design therapeutically important. However, existing molecular generation models often struggle to balance conflicting property requirements, maintain structural exploration, and avoid premature convergence during reinforcement learning. To address these challenges, we propose CMIR-RL, a reinforcement learning-based molecular generation model that integrates cooperative crossover-mutation exploration, structure-based intrinsic rewards, and Pareto-based multi-objective optimization. In CMIR-RL, mutation and crossover networks synergistically guide the agent to balance exploration and exploitation, while Pareto-front-guided reward assignment updates the generation policy under multiple property constraints. Experiments on a three-objective polypharmacology task show that CMIR-RL significantly improves desirability from 0.8868 to 0.9542 over the baseline method, while maintaining competitive validity, uniqueness, and diversity. Additional GuacaMol results further indicate competitive generalization across goal-directed molecular generation tasks. These results show that CMIR-RL is an effective reinforcement learning strategy for early-stage multi-objective molecular design.

records.title: Virus-like particle vaccines: from antigen architecture to antigen presentation and adaptive immune responses.
records.abstract: Virus-like particles (VLPs) mimic key structural features of native viruses while lacking a replication-competent viral genome, combining favorable safety with multivalent antigen presentation and strong immunogenicity. Yet, how VLP design influences the quality and persistence of adaptive immunity remains incompletely understood. This review examines relevant literature identified through targeted searches on recent advances in VLP engineering, with emphasis on particle architecture, antigen-display strategies, and structural determinants of immune recognition. We discuss how VLPs facilitate antigen presentation by antigen-presenting cells and shape CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell responses, immune memory, and T follicular helper cell-B-cell interactions within germinal centers. Emerging approaches linking VLP design with humoral and cellular immunity are also considered. The next generation of VLP vaccines will require a transition from empirical enhancement of immunogenicity toward precision engineering of immune responses. A major challenge is to establish robust and transferable structure-immunity relationships while addressing manufacturing feasibility, quality control, potency assessment, and product comparability. Advances in computational protein design, structural biology, and high-dimensional immune profiling are expected to enable increasingly quantitative and mechanism-based optimization of VLP platforms. However, fully predictive control over human immune responses will remain a complex challenge.

records.title: MolecureAI: an agentic AI platform for autonomous drug discovery.
records.abstract: Accelerating the identification of viable drug candidates across therapeutic areas demands autonomous systems for molecular generation that enforce chemical correctness by structural invariants rather than model capability. We present MolecureAI, an autonomous AI agent architecture for closed-loop drug discovery with cost-ordered cascade evaluation that addresses four capability gaps unresolved across the field: autonomous design strategy selection, persistent cross-campaign structural memory, in-loop ADMET safety gating, and literature-scale evidence integration into the generative loop. A cost-ordered cascade concentrates full structure-based evaluation on a small pre-filtered survivor set, achieving a 2.5 × reduction in candidates advanced relative to those generated. An in-loop metabolic gate enforces Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, and Toxicity (ADMET) safety by writing flagged reactive substructures to a per-target learned state, suppressing identified liabilities from all subsequent generation rounds. A persistent campaign memory influences generation trajectories by embedding prior structural success and failure patterns directly into the design context. We validate these architectural invariants across three structurally diverse benchmark targets (EGFR, KRAS G 12 C , and BRD4) through a five-condition component ablation and a controlled memory ablation, and confirm generator agnosticism across four language-model backends via a deterministic recalibration layer that overrides backend self-evaluation bias. Without explicit chemotype instruction, the pipeline computationally converged toward candidates bearing the 4-anilinoquinazoline scaffold characteristic of the approved inhibitors erlotinib and gefitinib, from structural feedback alone. Persistent campaign memory showed directional but non-significant trends toward lower inter-round score variance and higher late-stage advance rate ( n ≈ 90 per condition; all p > 0.20 ). The component ablation reveals that optimizing for a single objective collapses performance on others; only full orchestration resolves this tension. Advancement rates above 79% across all backends confirm that the validated properties are generator-agnostic, enforced by architectural invariants rather than model capability. All reported outcomes are properties of the computational generation process; prospective biochemical validation of the advanced candidates remains the primary direction for future work.

records.title: Functional alignment of protein language models via reinforcement learning.
records.abstract: Protein language models (pLMs) enable generative design of novel protein sequences but remain fundamentally misaligned with protein engineering goals, as they lack explicit understanding of function and often fail to improve properties beyond those found in nature. We introduce Reinforcement Learning from eXperimental Feedback (RLXF), a general framework that aligns protein language models with experimentally measured functional objectives, drawing inspiration from the methods used to align large language models like ChatGPT. Applied across five diverse protein families, RLXF improves generation of high-functioning variants beyond pre-trained baselines. We demonstrate this with CreiLOV, an oxygen-independent fluorescent protein, where RLXF-aligned models generate sequences with significantly enhanced fluorescence, including the most fluorescent CreiLOV variants reported to date. Our results indicate that RLXF-aligned models effectively integrate the evolutionary knowledge encoded in pre-trained pLMs with experimental observations, improving the success rate of generated sequences and enabling the discovery of synergistic mutation combinations that are difficult to identify through zero-shot or evolutionary approaches. RLXF provides a scalable and accessible approach to steer generative models toward desired biochemical properties, enabling function-driven protein design beyond the limits of natural evolution.

records.title: Decoding coupled epigenetic-fragmentomic signals in circulating cell-free DNA for interpretable cancer diagnosis.
records.abstract: Plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) whole-genome methylation sequencing enables simultaneous characterization of DNA methylation and fragmentomic features for cancer detection. However, it remains unclear whether methylation library preparation faithfully preserves fragmentomic signals, how methylation and fragmentation are biologically coupled, and how these two modalities can be systematically integrated. We systematically evaluated the preservation of cfDNA fragmentomic features in whole-genome bisulfite sequencing (WGBS) and enzymatic methyl sequencing (EM-seq) relative to conventional whole-genome sequencing (WGS). We next investigated the biological relationship between methylation and fragmentation and delineated methylation haplotype blocks (MHBs) directly from plasma cfDNA as biologically interpretable units for organizing multimodal cfDNA signals. Guided by these findings, we developed multimodal diagnostic models integrating complementary methylation and fragmentomic features. Canonical cfDNA fragmentomic patterns were partially preserved across methylation sequencing protocols, although the degree of preservation varied among individual features. DNA methylation levels were associated with characteristic fragment length and end-motif patterns. Plasma-derived MHBs exhibited tissue-associated regulatory features and distinct patterns of chromatin accessibility, repeat enrichment, and methylation heterogeneity, providing biologically interpretable units for integrated cfDNA analysis. Within these regions, methylation and fragmentomic signals exhibited coordinated yet complementary patterns. Leveraging this framework, we developed Fragmentomics And Methylation Ensemble (FAME), an interpretable multimodal model integrating MHB-centered methylation and fragmentomic features for cancer detection and tissue-of-origin prediction, and further extended it with complementary genome-wide methylation and fragmentomic features to generate a genome-wide-augmented FAME model (FAME-GW). Across cross-validation, independent validation, and comparisons with THEMIS (THorough Epigenetic Marker Integration Solution), SPOT-MAS (screening for the presence of tumor by methylation and size), and DELFI (DNA evaluation of fragments for early interception), FAME-based models achieved robust diagnostic performance, with FAME providing a compact and interpretable representation and FAME-GW delivering the strongest overall predictive performance. Our study demonstrates that cfDNA whole-genome methylation sequencing partially preserves informative fragmentomic signals and establishes plasma-derived MHBs as biologically interpretable units for organizing and integrating complementary methylation and fragmentomic information. This framework provides insight into the coupling of epigenetic and fragmentomic information and an effective strategy for interpretable cfDNA-based cancer diagnosis.

records.title: Value and research advances of ctDNA in perioperative therapy for non-small cell lung cancer.
records.abstract: Perioperative treatment plays an increasingly important role in improving outcomes for patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) offers a new perspective for optimizing individualized perioperative management. This review systematically examines the core value of ctDNA in perioperative therapy for resectable NSCLC, encompassing its correlation with treatment response and pathological remission during the neoadjuvant phase, its utility as a dynamic monitor of treatment efficacy, and its emerging role in prognostic stratification and recurrence prediction in the postoperative setting. Importantly, while ctDNA demonstrates considerable promise for guiding individualized perioperative management, most applications remain investigational; we therefore distinguish between established correlative uses and prospective strategies currently under evaluation in clinical trials. It also addresses current technical challenges in ctDNA application, including limited sensitivity, false positives, lack of standardization, cost-effectiveness concerns, and difficulties in integration into clinical decision-making. Future prospective interventional studies are needed to validate ctDNA-guided treatment adjustments and to establish standardized protocols and multidisciplinary collaboration pathways, thereby facilitating the integration of ctDNA into the full course of perioperative management for NSCLC and enabling precise efficacy assessment, risk stratification, and individualized treatment decisions.

records.title: Oral squamous cell carcinoma: A Modern Review of Pathogenesis and Treatment.
records.abstract: Oral cancer (OC), predominantly oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), is a serious global health burden with high mortality rates, especially in South and Southeast Asia. OC is a severe worldwide health issue that is mostly caused by a sedentary lifestyle, alcohol, tobacco, and areca nut intake. The highest prevalence of OSCC is in India and Southeast Asia. Complex genomic and epigenetic changes, such as TP53 dysfunction, enhanced EGFR alteration, and dysregulation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signalling pathways, in conjunction with tumor-promoting alterations in the tumor microenvironment, contribute to oral carcinogenesis ( Tan et al., 2023). Oral submucous fibrosis (a chronic condition that causes precancerous progression in mouth), and leukoplakia (white or grey patches to form on mucus membrane) are instances of oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMDs), which are key indicators of cancer conversion. Even with advances in histopathology and imaging, delayed diagnosis remains a major limitation. Salivary biomarkers, liquid biopsy devices, and artificial intelligence-based screening tools are examples of novel diagnostic methods with potential for early diagnosis. Therapeutically, novel approaches such as immunotherapy, targeted therapy, nanoparticle-based drug delivery systems, electro spun nanofibers, and plant-derived phytoformulations offer innovative, multi-targeted strategies with enhanced efficacy and reduce toxicity. However, surgery, radiation, and chemotherapy continue to be the primary treatment approaches. Improving new interventions for OC treatment needs a multifaceted approach that integrates early detection strategies, advanced therapeutic strategies, the use of plant-derived therapeutics, nanotechnology, artificial intelligence, and public health awareness to get better therapeutic outcomes.

records.title: Extracellular vesicle-based diagnosis of Mucormycosis: Candidate biomarkers, analytical challenges, and clinical translation.
records.abstract: Currently, no standard serological test is available for the detection of Mucorales. Mucormycosis is a rapidly progressing angioinvasive infection with a high mortality rate. However, since a diagnostically useful target (1 → 3)-β-D-glucan or Aspergillus galactomannan is not present in Mucorales, a negative result for such targets is a true negative and does not rule out the diagnosis of mucormycosis. PCR detection using PCR for Mucorales can be performed in the early stages, and there is a commercially available quantitative PCR kit in some places, although it is not uniform. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are membrane-bound particles present in biofluids that play a protective role against the degradation of proteins and nucleic acids and allow for their enrichment prior to measurement. Two studies provided evidence of Mucorales direct culture using extracellular RNA profiles from Rhizopus delemar and proteomic characterization of Mucor lusitanicus EVs, respectively; however, neither resulted in a patient-derived diagnostic test. This structured narrative review separates Mucorales EV direct evidence from extrapolations from other fungi and clinical EV assays. We recommend using a patient-derived discovery workflow involving EV-enriched RNA sequencing, EV-associated DNA analysis, and proteomics, followed by a locked multiplex assay of two or three independent fungal targets. Therefore, molecules from the CotH family, mucoricin, glucoamylase, iron-acquisition factors, and host-response signals should be considered as candidates and should be directly demonstrated within EVs from patients, rather than being considered as known EV markers.

records.title: Circulating citrullinated proteins as candidate liquid biopsy analytes in cancer.
records.abstract: This review outlines the functions of circulating citrullinated histone H3 (CitH3), citrullinated and matrix metalloproteinase-degraded vimentin (VICM), peptidylarginine deiminase 4 (PAD4), and related proteoforms in oncology and discusses their suitability as analytes in liquid biopsies. Evidence in the serum and plasma is different from that in the tissue, bone marrow, in vitro, or preclinical evidence. Special emphasis has been placed on the following techniques: serum and plasma-based enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), liquid chromatography - tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS), targeted proteomics, and biosensors. Evidence is best established for CitH3, but the biology of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) and their reported associations are context- and assay-dependent, with nucleosomal assays and assays of free histones/free peptides measuring distinct pools of analytes. However, for some cancers, these analytes have preliminary prognostic and treatment-response-monitoring value, but there is a lack of evidence for their clinical use in cancer diagnosis, patient stratification, or minimal residual disease (MRD) monitoring. Assay heterogeneity, matrix effects, lack of certified reference materials, limited inter-platform comparability and harmonization, lack of external quality assessment (EQA), and lack of validated clinical cut-offs hinder clinical implementation. Key preanalytical requirements include preanalytical control, harmonization of assays, assessment of the commutability of reference materials, calibrators, control materials, and EQA materials, and compliance with the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 15,189 and the In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation (IVDR). At present, citrullinated proteins should be considered as research use/early translational analytes, and not as clinically reportable oncology biomarkers.

records.title: Cell-free DNA fragmentomics and epigenomic profiling in hematologic malignancies: current evidence, translational limitations, and future directions.
records.abstract: Mutation-based liquid biopsy supports diagnosis and disease monitoring in hematologic malignancies, but interpretation of plasma variants may be complicated by clonal hematopoiesis, treatment-related changes, and nonmalignant blood-cell turnover. This structured narrative review evaluates whether cell-free DNA (cfDNA) fragmentomics, DNA methylation, and 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) provide complementary information beyond mutation detection. Direct plasma evidence is most developed for selected fragmentomic and 5hmC applications, although most studies remain retrospective, internally validated, or proof of concept. Fragmentomic studies have reported associations with lymphoma classification, outcome assessment, and longitudinal tumor-effector profiling during chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy, but routine clinical utility and decision thresholds are not established. Plasma 5hmC studies have reported associations with lymphoma classification, treatment response, prognosis, and measurable residual disease in acute myeloid leukemia, whereas pharmacodynamic monitoring during Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibition remains hypothesis-generating. DNA methylation may support source-cell or lineage inference, but lineage assignment does not establish malignant fraction, and key disease-assessment studies remain largely tissue-based, cellular-DNA-based, cross-cancer, or methodological. The novelty of this review is a structured evidence map that distinguishes direct plasma evidence from indirect support and compares the three modalities by biological information, assay compatibility, and validation maturity. We also propose a hypothesis-generating framework for sample-level integration using separate assay-specific aliquots and computational combination of outputs. No universal analytical order or clinically validated integrated workflow has been established. Fragmentomic and epigenomic profiling should therefore be regarded as investigational complements to mutation-based testing, requiring independent prospective validation against established genomic, cellular, imaging, and tissue-based methods.
